newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU extends safeguards against rice imports.
newsitem.headline: EU extends safeguards against rice imports.

text.p: The European Commission on Wednesday extended safeguard measures against rice imports from member states' overseas territories, setting a duty free tariff quota of 69,610 tonnes from May 1 to September 30, 1997.
The British territories of Montserrat and the Turks and Caicos Islands were allocated 10,000 tonnes with the remaining 59,610 tonnes for rice from other overseas territories.
Following a sharp increase in imports, the Commission set a limit of 44,278 tonnes from January 1 to April 30.
The imminent expiry of the safeguard measures risked creating a serious disturbance in the rice market, the Commission said in a statement.

In 1991 the EU agreed that rice produced in African, Caribbean and Pacific (ACP) member countries of the Lome convention could enjoy the free access granted to the EU's overseas countries and territories (OCT) after a small amount of processing.
Rice imported directly from ACP states benefits only from a 50 percent cut in customs duty within an annual quota of 125,000 tonnes.

Imports of rice from the overseas countries are expected to surge to 365,029 tonnes in 1996, from 58,000 tonnes in 1992, and would amount to more than their total production, a Commission official said.
The increase is mostly of rice processed in the Dutch Antilles but believed to come from the ACP states of Guyana and Surinam.
The new safeguard limit is based on annual average imports of 163,000 tonnes between 1992 and 1995.
